intent: Four additional families in every category, selected for varied rhythms, readable movement and score chasing. Enjoyment and cross-author difficulty handovers require playtesting.
overlapRule: Keep each variant's first four targets. Raise its two crossover targets toward stricter percentiles of its own board, with at least a one-point increase, capped to record minus one and record. Previously unreachable tails are repaired at that cap and explicitly identified. Expert has no outgoing overlap. Frozen before/after evidence lives in season_expansion_calibration.json.

families.focus: Sweep the room. Keep the magazine rolling.
families.why: Single-hit targets spread across three walls turn clicking into a room-clearing score chase. Reload-on-kill rewards a sustained rhythm. The four published Multiclick cuts widen the arena as difficulty rises.

families.focus: Pick your route through the gallery.
families.why: Vox's shooting-gallery layout offers route choice and quick successive kills. These Viscose click variants remove awkward spawns; Entry, Easier, Medium and Hard give the gallery a four-band progression.

families.focus: Chain the clears. Keep the rhythm alive.
families.why: Six-target reload clicking emphasizes a continuous clear-and-respawn rhythm. The first three cuts reduce target size; the Expert trustechain edit adds a different routing challenge. That final handover is a design choice requiring playtesting.

families.focus: Find a three-target beat and build speed.
families.why: Three close static targets create short, repeatable chains with little travel time. Larger 80%, Larger, standard and 10% small provide a size progression for a compact score-chasing circuit.

families.focus: Catch the next head as it drifts into view.
families.why: Floating heads in a layered arena offer a shooting-gallery rhythm with depth changes. Viscose's Entry through Hard edits supply a coherent four-band progression without replacing the core Pasu and Popcorn tests.

families.focus: Hop between layers. Catch each passing dot.
families.why: Far moving dots at several vertical layers turn the run into a layered gallery. The Goated Easier, Medium, Hard and Expert edits retain the same scene while changing the challenge.

families.focus: Ride the wave from shot to shot.
families.why: SunClick and WaveClick add a timing-focused wave circuit with a repeatable rhythm. This is a mixed-release progression using Aimerz's Easy S1, Normal, Hard and Hard S1 cuts; its handovers need playtesting.

families.focus: Catch the leap. Reload on every clear.
families.why: Four single-click bots leap across a flat surface at different depths. A three-shot magazine refills on each kill, creating an arcade-like clear-and-reload loop. The four published Bounceshot cuts keep that loop across the bands.

families.focus: Follow the bounce all the way to the corner.
families.why: The DVD-inspired moving target gives continuous tracking a recognizable screen-bounce motif. MASSIVE, Big, standard and Small keep the motion theme while reducing the target size.

families.focus: Trace the flower. Stay with each little turn.
families.why: The author's bee-collecting-pollen theme gives compact tracking a playful identity. Entry, Easier, standard and Hard keep the Flower motion across the four bands. The scenario name is not a requirement to change sensitivity.

families.focus: Cruise with the dot as it circles you.
families.why: A gently jumping dot flying around the player adds a flowing orbital chase. Viscose's Horizontal Entry, Easier, standard and Hard cuts expand the motion challenge while keeping the same visual theme.

families.focus: Sweep around the dish in one flowing motion.
families.why: Wide sweeping strafes in a circular dish give tracking a distinctive arena and long flowing paths. The four published Snake Track bands provide a consistent scene from Novice through Expert.

families.focus: Stay ready for the next strange turn.
families.why: Air Spectral's deliberately unusual Air movement adds a surprise-driven chase. Easy 85%, Easy, standard and Harder retain that theme. Its terse author description supports the unusual-motion intent, not a claim of measured enjoyment.

families.focus: Follow the aerial course through every phase.
families.why: Air Divine-style movement brings a longer aerial course into the season. Easy Slowed, Easy, No UFO and Harder progress from a slowed course to the full challenge; the final UFO handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Air CELESTIAL No UFO Easy Slowed

families.focus: Clear the full aerial gauntlet.
families.why: The full Air scenario changes phases within a run, unlike the existing single-bot Air Reading circuit. Published Novice through Elite variants make this a varied endurance chase with a clear finish.

families.focus: Stay close. Catch the reversal.
families.why: A close strafing opponent adds a grounded duel-like chase beside the aerial courses. Easy Thin, standard, Thin and Precise+ are a proposed progression; speed and size both change, so the first handover needs playtesting.
rungs: Close Fast Strafes Easy Invincible - Thin

families.focus: Clear the room in fast bursts.
families.why: Stationary Vox targets reward route choice and rapid full-auto clears without movement reading. Jumbo, standard, Small and xxSmall turn the room into a four-band switching sprint.

families.focus: Pass from wave to wave without losing pace.
families.why: Smoothly drifting targets give switching a visible wave rhythm. Community Benchmarks' easy cut leads into Revosect Entry, Intermediate and standard. The cross-author first handover is provisional.

families.focus: Sweep the sky one target at a time.
families.why: Slow horizontal targets at several depths make a readable aerial switching gallery. Four published skyTS bands keep the movement predictable while increasing the target challenge.

families.focus: Burst through the pack. Find the next clear.
families.why: Low-FOV target switching concentrates the action into short, fast clears. Easy, NR, rAim and NR Small are a proposed cross-edit progression; the two middle releases need an in-game difficulty comparison.

families.focus: Chase the drift between the two chambers.
families.why: Four jumping and floating targets in layered chambers give each run an arena-clearing loop. The published DriftTS Novice through Elite scenarios supply a consistent four-band progression.

families.focus: Chase the bouncing crowd around the pentagon.
families.why: Five targets bounce across a pentagonal wall and each needs a short sustained burst to clear. This adds an arena-like switching loop with plenty of target choice. The four published Season 5 cuts provide exact variants for every band.

families.focus: Clear the floating pack, one target at a time.
families.why: Four gently jumping and floating targets share a narrow chamber, producing a compact clear-the-room loop. The four published ControlTS bands keep the same arena and short sustained bursts throughout the progression.

families.focus: Flow into the next moving target.
families.why: Smooth transfer adds longer flowing target-to-target routes beside the sharper evasive circuits. Community Benchmarks' easy cut leads into Revosect's three SmoothTS tiers. The first cross-author handover needs playtesting.
